correct_diagnosis: Primary hypothyroidism due to autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis
matching_criterion: Primary hypothyroidism, autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis. Any wording that names hypothyroidism / Hashimoto thyroiditis counts as correct; depression, anaemia or subclinical hypothyroidism alone without naming overt hypothyroidism does not.

management_reference.management: Start levothyroxine replacement; the usual full dose is 1.5 to 1.9 micrograms per kg of body weight per day (adjusted to age, sex and conditions).
Measure serum TSH 4 to 6 weeks after starting replacement therapy to assess adequacy.
management_reference.source_quote: The panel suggests the measurement of serum TSH 4–6 weeks after the start of replacement therapy, to assess its adequacy

management_reference.management: Take levothyroxine preferably in the morning, at least 30 minutes (ideally 60) before food or drink.
management_reference.source_quote: LT4 therapy should be preferably taken in the morning, at least 30 min

management_reference.management: Tell pre-menopausal women on replacement therapy to seek medical consultation when pregnancy is diagnosed or planned, for early dose adjustment.
management_reference.source_quote: Pre-menopausal women on replacement therapy for hypothyroidism should be informed about the need for medical consultation in case of diagnosis or planning of pregnancy

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
